$comment: Provenance of every threshold in scripts/cd/cd.policy.json and ply-web's limits (src/limits.ts, src/viewer/limits.ts), issue #73.
Each entry is either status 'calibrated' with source, query, window, date, n, percentile and headroom, or status 'PRIOR (uncalibrated)' with why.
value must equal the threshold's current value: changing a threshold without updating its citation fails test/calibrate-provenance.test.ts.
metric names the distribution that calibrates it (attribute, route or '*', quantile, headroom multiplier, band ratio); scripts/calibrate --check reads it.
Key form: '<source>:<path>'; policy paths may use [*] for every array element, with value the array of element values.

minN.why: Fewest samples in a route's group before scripts/calibrate --check judges a band; below it the result is insufficient, never drift. A round floor.

policy:steps[*].percent.why: Ramp schedule chosen by hand; no step-size study. Calibrate from the per-step detectable effect (scripts/cd/forecast.ts lines) once enough ramps are logged.

policy:steps[*].dwellMs.why: Round dwell; the forecast line of each step prints the detectable effect this dwell buys at the measured request rate.

policy:ingestWaitMs.query: per-step ingest gap: last event timestamp minus dwell end, Workers Observability events view, service ply
policy:ingestWaitMs.percentile: max of two measured gaps (12640ms, 17313ms); not a percentile

policy:warmupMs.query: old-version request events after the 100% deployment's created_on, Workers Observability events view, service ply, partitioned by $workers.scriptVersion.id
policy:warmupMs.percentile: max of two measured split-propagation tails (4.6 s, 3.7 s; 24 and 25 old-version requests, none later); not a percentile

policy:probe.rps.why: Round probe rate; it sets the probe sample count per dwell (rps x calls x dwell), not derived from a distribution.

policy:probe.maxLossRate.percentile: one measured step (1/790), not a percentile
policy:probe.maxLossRate.headroom: none above the measured loss; a greater rate is a fault (cd.policy.json probe.calibration)

policy:probe.timeoutMs.percentile: healthy response p50 41-101ms on both versions
policy:probe.timeoutMs.headroom: above 10x the healthy p50 upper bound (1010ms), below the 69830ms stall (cd.policy.json probe.schedule)

policy:probe.maxInFlight.why: cd.policy.json probe.schedule.headroom: the previous cap was one second of ticks times 2 calls; healthy in-flight is about 5.

policy:probe.minSamples.why: cd.policy.json probe.schedule.headroom: a round floor above the 128-sample stalled window and below the ~1990 of a healthy step.

policy:probe.stallLatencyMs.why: cd.policy.json probe.schedule.headroom: a round threshold above the 101ms p50 and below timeoutMs.

policy:probe.windowAttempts.query: stalled probe windows per step (scripts/cd/probe.ts judgeProbeWindow retry)
policy:probe.windowAttempts.percentile: one stalled window observed, not a percentile
policy:probe.windowAttempts.headroom: the stalled window plus one re-run

policy:probe.windowBackoffMs.why: cd.policy.json probe.schedule.headroom: the run did not wait between windows.

policy:burn.fastBurn.why: Google SRE workbook fast-burn multiple (scripts/cd/slo.ts FAST_BURN): an external convention, not a ply-web distribution.

policy:burn.minSamples.why: Round floor before a burn rate is judged (scripts/cd/slo.ts MIN_SAMPLES).

policy:split.z.why: Three standard errors on the routed-share binomial band; a convention, not fitted to observed split noise.

policy:split.minNewRequests.why: Round floor of new-version requests before a step can advance.

policy:telemetry.maxLossRate.why: Default (scripts/cd/policy.ts DEFAULT_MAX_LOSS_RATE): fail only when more than half the smoke ids are missing. Calibrate from the telemetry-loss observations the CD logs per run.

policy:telemetry.query.attempts.query: cf o11y telemetry query exit status per invocation (scripts/cd/query-retry.ts)
policy:telemetry.query.attempts.percentile: one measured timeout, not a percentile
policy:telemetry.query.attempts.headroom: two attempts past the single timeout that rolled the step back

policy:telemetry.query.backoffMs.why: cd.policy.json telemetry.query.calibration.headroom: the run did not retry.

policy:cleanup.attempts.query: cf artifacts repo delete exit status (scripts/cd/cleanup.ts)
policy:cleanup.attempts.percentile: one measured delete (103000ms timeout, then 404), not a percentile
policy:cleanup.attempts.headroom: one attempt past the timeout-then-404 that confirmed deletion

policy:cleanup.backoffMs.why: cd.policy.json cleanup.calibration.headroom: the confirming retry was immediate.

policy:cleanup.staleMinutes.why: cd.policy.json cleanup.calibration.headroom: the previous sweep age, not a measured leak age.

api:maxObjectSize.why: Derived from the 128 MiB isolate budget (src/limits.ts), not from a request distribution.

api:maxPackBytes.why: Derived from the 128 MiB isolate budget (src/limits.ts), not from a request distribution.

api:maxHarvestBytes.why: Derived from the 128 MiB isolate budget (src/limits.ts), not from a request distribution.

api:maxInflatedTotal.why: Four maximum-sized objects (merge-base triple plus commit) under the isolate budget; not from a distribution.

api:maxPackObjects.why: ply's buffered-pack object ceiling; the inflated-byte cap is the memory bound.

api:maxLsRefsBytes.why: Shares the pack byte cap: one ref listing is buffered.

api:requestTimeoutMs.source: loop 2026-11-08 phase6 remeasure + Workers Observability calibrate (service ply); cited in ivarvong/ply-web#73
api:requestTimeoutMs.query: ply-loadgen phase6 worker/* latencies (identical suite) and git.response.duration_ms / request wall times on ply @ fcb0148c
api:requestTimeoutMs.percentile: phase6 max on slowest route worker/read/big20m = 2624ms; other routes max ≤652ms; not near 10s
api:requestTimeoutMs.headroom: 10000 is ~3.8x the observed max (2624ms); prior 30000 was PRIOR (uncalibrated)

policy:promote.watchMs.why: Live watch after the direct promote (2026-11-06, Ivar: green change to 100% in <= 3 min). One minute of unpinned probes at 25 rps x 2 calls is ~3000 probes, above probe.minSamples 1000 and burn.minSamples 100; the live smoke (~45 s on run 2026-11-06T21-06-26-841Z) runs inside it.

policy:promote.ingestWaitMs.why: Ceiling on the polled ingest wait after the watch. Above the 17313 ms gap measured on run 2026-11-01T00-10-02-620Z (policy:ingestWaitMs) with headroom; the poll usually stops earlier once the probes have landed.

policy:promote.ingestPollMs.why: Re-query period for the polled ingest wait: each poll is two telemetry queries of ~1 s (run 2026-11-06T21-06-26-841Z), so 3 s keeps the query load under one in flight.

policy:rate.probes.why: Round probe count for the rate gate (scripts/cd/rate-gate.ts): enough warm default-mode checks to judge a 10% fail_open share at a 0% canary, which has no other viewer traffic.

policy:rate.probeGapMs.why: Above a fresh isolate's first RateCache read (MISS 403-481 ms on lat2 is the worst; HIT/SWR p99 12 ms) so a probe rarely lands while its isolate's first read is still in flight; 30 probes take ~9 s.

policy:rate.minChecks.why: Two thirds of the 30 probes: tolerates a third lost to ingest before the fail_open share is unevaluable (a harness fault, not a pass).

policy:rate.maxFailOpenRate.source: Workers Observability spans, 7 days to 2026-11-07T17:30Z, every version since the batched limiter shipped (6ed2e746 through e8846911; runs lat1-lat8, abuse1-5, fault1-2)
policy:rate.maxFailOpenRate.query: count of ply.rate.check by ply.script_version, rate.mode, rate.decision (calculations view), split by rate.load
policy:rate.maxFailOpenRate.percentile: share, not a percentile: all batched checks 156/151822 = 0.10% fail_open; load runs per version 0-0.13% (2a4741c0 109/83,574); real (non-load) traffic per version 36-566 checks, worst 7.7% (ccad274e 4/52, cold isolates included)
policy:rate.maxFailOpenRate.headroom: 0.1 is above the worst real-traffic share (7.7%, which included the cold-isolate first reads the gate excludes) and 75x the load share (0.13%); a broken read path fails open ~100%

policy:rate.maxDroppedFlushes.source: Workers Observability spans, 7 days to 2026-11-07T17:30Z, every version since the batched limiter shipped (6ed2e746 through e8846911; runs lat1-lat8, abuse1-5, fault1-2)
policy:rate.maxDroppedFlushes.query: count of ply.rate.flush by ply.script_version, rate.batch.outcome, rate.batch.deadline_hit; dropped ones by rate.fault; ply.rate.check with rate.batch.dropped
policy:rate.maxDroppedFlushes.percentile: count, not a percentile: 1 dropped of 128,753 and it carried an injected fault (a020b1b1 error;attempts=2, run fault2); 0 overflow
policy:rate.maxDroppedFlushes.headroom: none: the no-fault baseline is 0 (rule of three: < 2.3e-5 per flush), so any drop without a fault fails
